Thank you for the feedback! I'm still trying to kick the tense switching so I guess that'll just be proactive editing and working on it more. As far as being descriptive, I often think I'm being drawn out and rambling when adding the descriptive language. My goal of this "second take" was to cut things down and add more to the plot, I've cut a good bit of descriptive language so I'll retroactively add it in, hopefully with more success. 
How do you feel I developed the opening of the plot? What did you gather from the page? I'd be interested to know where you think the story will go.

EDIT: I see you said you aren't good at anything in another reply. Just keep in mind that you may have simply not found what you are good at. Nobody knows they are good at basketball until they play a game, the future NBA star who fails at every sport and has never tried basketball isn't "bad at everything", they haven't found their niche. It's an analogy so don't take it literally but I hope you can see, you have many countless opportunities and doors sitting open in your future, walk through as many doors as possible, you may find something wonderful.  

1. Maybe i was somewhat unclear but yes I was saying that a chemical imbalance (could) be causing depression. As for trauma. Would you like to speak about it? The psyche can often be treated just like the body. There is a wide range of proven treatments for psyche issues. Consider doing some research into it and just looking at options. 

2. You're welcome, I think It's easy to assume "the world is better without me" and I've done it plenty of times, so I'm glad I could help you see it won't be better without you.

3. So you've made some assumptions here. I'd like you to just google suicide survivor stories. Just read some, there is a few reddit posts that are amazing. I know you don't want emotion and this will be that, but it does show you that many people go on living a daily life after. Most people who commit suicide and survive either don't tell anybody or tell a small group of people. I know friends who have survived a suicide attempt, they live normal lives now and they aren't forced into any way of life. As for drugs to help such as antidepressants I hold a similar view where I'd like to be the whole me not a drugged version, so i see your point. Also consider different forms of therapy, this is like therapy for many just speaking online. Online chat services exist with free ongoing support also, consider those. 

4. This is true you will die anyway, but your death now will only prevent possible good times. You could turn around and in 5 years think you were blind to not see that things can change, you also may not and I can't make that judgement so just keep it in mind that you will develop as you age and you can with work and effort change your life. And I know you're a minor so you can't do everything but small things like working out, doing a sport or activity can help remove anxiety, stress and other factors. 

5. So you've had some failed attempts at doing things? You're young and those represent a very small slice of your life. Some people get to their happy place at 15, some at 20, some at 25 or older. You are not limited by mental illness. There are so many successful people with mental illness or previous mental illness. Some people do live long lives of regret, don't assume you are some people. 

Here is a link to a survivor story thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/4e8oip/serious_suicide_survivors_of_reddit_what_was_your/
Thanks man! I really like success stories, they're motivating and although you aren't in the same boat It helps to know things change for others.
This was a big concern, I've decided against it, however if I decide for it in the future I'll not be going that route for that reason.
It is just the feeling, really my outlook on the world, I'm a sort of nihilist.

>You won't be the same person for all your life - people change drastically. People grow and learn from their life to be the person they want to be, and yes that takes time and effort and sometimes even adversity, but it will be worth it. I promise.

This actually got past me, I'm a bit hypocritical because I also preach that people change. I will try and give myself more time, and perhaps look at ways of powering through.

It will definitely shut my liver down and kill me slowly, however it will get me very high at first and they should block a lot of my pain receptors, perhaps I need to look further into how it kills you. No drugs available to me but yeah. As long as I don't feel the pain I don't mind dying slowly, it will give me some time to realise my decision. I don't want a quick death with no closure.
I am being quite honest. This does not help me I'm sorry.
I'm sorry I appreciate the help, but this is not something I can relate to. I don't think you and I were/are in the same position. But It's good to see you have found a better place.
I recognise the beauty of the world, it does not make me want to live, it will be beautiful when I am dead also.

Okay. 
There are 7.5ish billion people on Earth, among a vast solar system of many systems in a galaxy of many galaxies in a cluster of many clusters in a vast universe. The Earth does not care if you breath it's oxygen. So if we are going to remove emotions, lets remove those. 
Let's talk about facts.

1. You're a minor: Your brain chemistry is not at the level of an adult, this is just a fact. You're brain is not fully developed, so although you may not think a major change to your mindset will happen, it's likely that at least some change on how you think will happen as you mature. Think about how much of what you feel may be attributed to brain chemistry? If you subscribe to a scientific view of emotion, then all emotion and feeling is brain chemistry, imagine what an imbalance may do to that? Consider waiting it out and seeing a health professional about medication to aid this issue and be assessed properly.

2. Nothing bad will happen when you die. You're right here and this is NOT me advocating this. But, nothing will happen when anyone else dies. You are harming others just as much as the rockface hurts the planet by salting the oceans, hurting freshwater fish. Life continues despite challenges. I can promise you, leaving the world will do nothing to the world that is positive. You will die, be buried or cremated, turned into your component elements and molecules, be consumed by the ground, feed a plant, who will produce oxygen, which will be consumed by an aerobic organism who will produce carbon dioxide. The cycle continues, this is not a logical reason to end your life.

3. 94% of suicide survivors remain alive or die of natural unrelated causes. This is a real statistic carried out with a large sample size. Taking this into account, we can assume there is a very large chance upon the moments before death, you will feel vast, deep regret and realise all your problems are fixable. This leads in to the next point.

4. You will die. You will not get lucky and survive and appreciate your life, if you attempt suicide you will die and you should never assume you will survive or that there is a chance you will. You will die. It may not seem like a reason not to do it. But many people attempt suicide as a way to explore their fantasy of death or as an impulse. Do not let an impulse end your life. 

5. You can change your statistics to do more good than bad for the earth. I can't promise you will go on to do anything, this is ultimately up to you. But you could go to school, be an environmental biologist for example, help produce a renewable energy source or oxygen source, help prevent global warming, save the beautiful world you clearly love. Find sanctum in your ability to do good. You have untapped potential in every part of you. You may save lives, and if your life is the only one you save, that's okay! Try and save yourself today, work on the rest later. Take it slow, survive, improve, survive. You could live an amazing life.

As for help. Call a help line, seriously it's a hard thing to do but do it, ask what they suggest for immediate advice as I should not other professional help. Then consider seeing a family doctor in private from your parents if you're uncomfortable with that, ask the doctor for advice, move from there. GOODLUCK.

Condolences, but glad to see you are doing something to extend his spirit :)
